editorial.title: From question to reproducible evidence
editorial.subtitle: ANES96 · conditional associations in observational data
editorial.abstract: A methods example examining TV-news frequency alongside age, education, urban scale and party group. Fix the sample, measurement units, model, uncertainty and limits of interpretation together.

figure.caption: Pele 1.6.0 layout. Arrows indicate the analysis procedure, not causality.

sections.title: 01 / Sample and measurement
body: 944 respondents. Unweighted exploratory analysis; not a population estimate for US voters. TV news is measured in times/week; the age coefficient is per 10 years.

sections.title: 03 / Interpretation boundary
body: Party group was not randomized. Neither regression coefficients nor path directions identify a causal effect. Assess selection, measurement and omitted factors separately.

sections.title: 04 / Reuse with another manuscript
body: Do not replace the sample size alone. Update the data version, units, denominators, estimand, model and uncertainty calculation, then cross-check each figure ID against the source.

references: Pele 1.6.0 · https://pele.run/ · data and rendering contributions are distinguished.
